title: Experiences of entrustable professional activity assessment workload among residents, assessors and administrators: a qualitative study in an internal medicine residency
abstract: Purpose: to understand how residents, faculty assessors, chief residents and administrators experience the workload of EPA assessment and why assessments are late, brief or strategically chosen. Method: semi-structured interviews and two focus groups, October 2026 to March 2027, analysed with reflexive thematic analysis. Results and conclusions will be written after analysis.
introduction: Competency-based residencies rely on frequent workplace-based assessment, and programmes set minimum numbers without agreed evidence. Retrieved studies describe residents managing targets strategically and assessors completing forms late from memory, but few studies ask residents, assessors and administrators together.
methods: Purposive sampling across training years, graduate background and assessment counts; interviews by a research assistant without a progression role; focus groups in protected time; reflexive thematic analysis by two analysts with a reflexive log. Ethics approval REB-2026-0412.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present themes with supporting quotations by role, a table of participants by role and training year, and participants' proposals for the assessment target.
discussion: The discussion will relate the themes to the retrieved accounts of strategic requesting and late completion, consider what they imply for the June target review, and state what a single-programme study cannot show.
limitations: One programme; accounts may be shaped by the programme audience; residents with the most difficult experiences may be under-represented.
conclusion: To be written after analysis; it will describe mechanisms and proposals and will not claim that any target change works.
summary: COREQ-structured draft with results left empty until analysis.
